title: Ada and the Salt
premise: Cyrus Marchetti, an exiled storm-caller hiding in the magic-free city of Vell, is handed a dying stranger's map to the Salt Door—the last passage out of Ostrava, a country that was erased from every record and border five years ago. Pursued by the Gray Wardens who enforce the ban on magic, Cyrus reluctantly gathers a found family: Ada, a salt-seller's daughter who can taste lies; Bramble, a disgraced cartographer; and the ghost of the dead stranger, Wren, who rides in Cyrus's memory. As they cross a landscape that literally forgets them, Cyrus learns the Door doesn't lead out of Ostrava—it leads back into its true name, and opening it will restore the country at the cost of Cyrus's own remembered identity. In the end, Cyrus chooses to give up their name so that Ostrava—and everyone in it—can be remembered again, waking as a stranger welcomed home by the family that chose to stay.
about_author: Petra Voss is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper turned novelist who writes about borders, weather, and the people who fall between them. She lives on a cold coast with two dogs and an unreasonable number of maps.

chapters.title: Charms for a City Without Weather
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. We meet Cyrus selling rain-charms that don't work in Vell, where magic is outlawed and storm-callers are hunted. A routine day curdles when a Gray Warden nearly catches them charming a fevered child. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: The Stranger at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses into Cyrus's stall at dusk, presses a salt-crusted map into their hands, and dies whispering 'the Door remembers.' The Wardens arrive; Cyrus flees with the map and a stolen coat. Emotional beat: terror and unwanted inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with Wren's ghost flickering in memory. The map shows roads that no longer exist and a coastline erased from every atlas. Cyrus realizes the dead man came from Ostrava—their own vanished homeland. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing like a tide.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Tasted Lies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada, a salt-seller's daughter, catches Cyrus lying about their name by the taste of it on the air. Instead of reporting them, she offers passage on her father's barge—for a price: the truth. Emotional beat: wary curiosity becoming alliance.

chapters.title: Downriver, Against Every Law
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The barge slips past Warden checkpoints while Ada's father pretends to haul salt. Wren's ghost grows stronger near old Ostravan stones, guiding them toward the first waypoint. Emotional beat: the fragile warmth of traveling with allies.

chapters.title: Bramble and the Blank Country
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. They recruit Bramble, a disgraced royal cartographer imprisoned for mapping Ostrava after its erasure. He confirms the horrifying truth: the country isn't hidden—it has been unmade from memory itself. Emotional beat: vindication twisted into dread.

chapters.title: The First Forgetting
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Crossing the boundary region, Ada briefly forgets her father's face and Bramble loses his mother tongue for an hour. The land eats memory the deeper they go. Emotional beat: fear that the journey will hollow them out.

chapters.title: Wren, Whole and Broken
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (ghost chapters begin). Wren recalls dying at the Salt Door and entrusting the map to 'the one who called storms.' Wren hid something from Cyrus in life—a betrayal tied to the exile five years ago. Emotional beat: guilt beyond the grave.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Knew My Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Warden-Captain Ilsa Rehn corners them at a ferry crossing—but instead of arresting Cyrus, she reveals she also came from Ostrava and forgot she had. She lets them go, shaken. Emotional beat: enemy revealed as fellow exile.

chapters.title: Salt on the Tongue
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada confesses her secret: she can taste lies because she was born on the Salt Door's threshold, making her half-key, half-lock. The group realizes the Door needs her blood to open. Emotional beat: the burden of being needed for what you are.

chapters.title: The City That Eats Travelers
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. They shelter in Meridian, a town of people the erasure spat out—half-remembered citizens living in buildings that fade at dawn. Here Cyrus finds someone who remembers their true name, and it isn't Marchetti. Emotional beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Rehn's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. The Captain tracks them again, torn between duty and the hole in her heart where Ostrava should be. She offers safe passage in exchange for being taken along to the Door. Emotional beat: a hunter asking to be saved.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Shallows
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Wardens ambush the group at the tidal flats. Cornered, Cyrus breaks their five-year vow and calls a storm—saving Ada, dooming their anonymity. Emotional beat: exhilaration and self-betrayal entwined.

chapters.title: What Wren Hid
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The full confession: Wren helped design the erasure, believing it would end a war, then repented too late. The map is both apology and trap—the Door demands a life freely given. Emotional beat: remorse seeking absolution it cannot earn.

chapters.title: The Long Cold Road
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The party crosses the Unmapped Reach, where Bramble's maps redraw themselves nightly. Ada begins forgetting pieces of her childhood; she asks Cyrus to remember her for her. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened by mortality.

chapters.title: Rehn's Choice
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Reinforced Wardens close in. Rehn turns on her own soldiers to buy the group a night's head start, knowing it ends her career—or her life. Emotional beat: loyalty finally finding its object.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. They reach the Salt Door: a seam of white stone in a cliff that exists only when no one looks directly at it. Wren's ghost manifests fully and explains the price—one soul must be forgotten entirely to anchor the restoration. Emotional beat: awe collapsing into horror.

chapters.title: Every Hand Raised Against the Tide
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The final Warden assault hits as Ada cuts her palm on the Door. Each companion volunteers to be the one forgotten; each argues why it shouldn't be another. Emotional beat: love expressed as argument over sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Name I Give Away
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus understands at last: the erasure took their homeland because Cyrus, the strongest storm-caller, fled rather than anchor it. They step forward and speak their true name into the Door, surrendering it. Emotional beat: acceptance, grief, and fierce resolve.

chapters.title: Ostrava Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Light floods the coast; borders redraw, bells ring in a city reborn, and Wren's ghost dissolves forgiven. But Cyrus is gone from every mind—including Ada's, who now carries only a salt-stained map and an ache she can't explain. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later, a nameless storm-caller washes ashore with no past. Ada tastes no lie when they say they feel they've come home. She takes them to her father's barge, and the family reforms around the empty space shaped like Cyrus. Emotional beat: found family choosing again.

chapters.title: Ada and the Salt
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, fragmentary. On the barge at dawn, watching Ada laugh, Cyrus feels memories surfacing like drowned things—the storm, the Door, the name given away. Whether it all returns or never does, they are home, and the salt on the wind tastes like beginning. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won hope.
